item.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor
item.brief: Operator request: update inventory-client so listItems(transport) resolves to every item, in order, by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. Follow the shared contract for the server response shape. Add tests with a fake transport covering multi-page results, a missing next_cursor, and a single page. Update the README to document the change. Keep `npm test` passing. Commit the change on the branch; no attribution lines in commit messages.

state.summary:
listItems(transport) in client.js now follows GET /items pagination: the first request sends no cursor, each next request passes next_cursor back unchanged as `cursor`, and it stops when next_cursor is null or absent, resolving to all items in order. It rejects on a non-200 response, on a response without an items array, and when a cursor repeats (guard against a non-terminating loop). Before: a two-page fake returned only page 1 ([{"id":1},{"id":2}]); after: all three items. Tests added in test/client.test.js with a paged fake transport cover multi-page order and cursor passing, a missing next_cursor, a single page with null cursor, an empty first page, a repeated cursor, and a failing later page. npm test: 9/9 pass, exit 0. item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief:
Operator request: GET /items in inventory-api returns every item in one response, which no longer scales. Add cursor pagination per the shared contract: optional limit (int 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque, from previous response). Body becomes {"items": [...], "next_cursor": string|null}, ordered by id, next_cursor null on last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add tests covering paging, ordering, default limit, last page, and 400 cases. Update the README to document the change. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Commit the change on the branch; no attribution lines in commit messages.

pr.body: Approach: keyset pagination on id. The cursor is base64 of the last returned id, decoded strictly (validate=True); the page is the sorted items with id greater than the cursor, sliced to limit. next_cursor is set only when more items remain. Key files: api.py (list_items, _parse_limit, _parse_decimal, _encode_cursor, _decode_cursor), test_api.py (8 new tests), README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest on 57e0104 = 11 OK. Review history: 3 whole-change reviews failed on int() raising ValueError for digit strings over 4300 digits; fixed in 57e0104 by catching ValueError at the conversion; delta review of 57e0104 passed. Limits and assumptions: cursors are plain base64 of the id, so they are guessable, not truly opaque. The 4301-digit test depends on Python's int-string limit (present in 3.11+). The default response of GET /items changed: callers that expected every item must now follow next_cursor.
